findings.title: Balance API trusts user_id from the request body
findings.attacker: Any Telegram user who opens the Mini App, or anyone with curl. No special access needed.
trace: webapp/src/api.js:12 sends { user_id: Telegram.WebApp.initDataUnsafe.user.id } in the request body
server/routes/balance.js:18 reads req.body.user_id and loads that user's wallet; initData is never validated on this route
POST /api/withdraw with another user's id moves their balance to the caller's card
findings.impact: Read and withdraw any user's balance. Full account takeover of the wallet feature.
findings.fix: Send `Authorization: tma ${Telegram.WebApp.initData}`, validate it in a middleware (HMAC with key HMAC_SHA256('WebAppData', BOT_TOKEN), auth_date ≤ 1h), and use the validated user.id. Ignore user_id from the body.
findings.verified_by: verifier-2 (fresh context, re-read routes and middleware registration)

findings.title: Webhook may accept forged updates
findings.unresolved: set_webhook is called without secret_token; whether the nginx config in front of the bot restricts the webhook path to Telegram's IP ranges is not in the repository.

findings.title: innerHTML in the splash screen
findings.rejection_reason: The assigned value is a static SVG string defined in the same file; no user, URL or API data reaches it.
